200.description: Logged in; sets session, refresh and CSRF cookies

post.summary:
Idempotent and keyed off the refresh cookie (see `IdentityService::logout`): logging out with
no cookie, an already-revoked cookie, or a garbage cookie all just clear client cookies and
return `204`, matching the anti-enumeration style used elsewhere in this module. Also acts on
an ambient cookie, so it needs the CSRF double-submit check too.

"Log out everywhere": revokes every refresh session for the caller and clears this
browser's cookies. Needs a live session (it acts on the user, not one refresh token) and
the CSRF check. Other devices' access cookies lapse within `ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL` (15 min).

Always `202` with the same message, whether or not the email exists (US-03) -- the identity
service already enforces this at the service layer, this handler just can't turn it into a
non-generic error either.

202.description: Same response whether or not the email exists

post.summary:
Keys off the refresh cookie, not `SessionClaims` -- a still-valid refresh token should be
usable to get a new access cookie even after the old access cookie has already expired,
which is the whole point of having a separate, longer-lived refresh token (US-02). Acts
purely on an ambient cookie, so it's one of the two routes that need the CSRF double-submit
check (see `crate::csrf`).

200.description: Rotated; sets new session, refresh and CSRF cookies

patch.summary:
Profile settings. Acts on the ambient session cookie, so it takes the CSRF double-submit

post.summary:
Confirms chunk `idx` is uploaded, with its size and SHA-256. Idempotent on
`(take_id, idx)`: the same size and hash again is a no-op; a different one is `409`.

404.description: No such take, or not the caller's

409.description: Acked before with a different hash or size, or the take is finalized

422.description: Not uploaded, size differs from storage, or invalid size/hash/index

post.summary:
Presigned `PUT` URLs for chunk `idx` (and, with `?count=`, the chunks after it). Only the
recording's owner gets them, and only until the take is finalized. The browser then `PUT`s
the bytes straight to object storage (media never passes through the API).

parameters.name: count
parameters.description:
How many consecutive chunk URLs to return, starting at `idx` (1–10, default 1). Used to
batch round trips after a reconnect.

404.description: No such take, or not the caller's

422.description: count outside 1–10 or index too large

post.summary:
Declares the take complete. When every chunk `0..chunk_count` is acknowledged the take is
finalized, the recording moves to `processing` and `TakeFinalized` is emitted; otherwise
`422` lists the missing indexes. Retrying a successful finalize is `202` again.

402.description: Longer than the plan allows (free tier: 10 minutes)

404.description: No such take, or not the caller's

409.description: Finalized before with another count, or the recording no longer accepts uploads

422.description: Chunks missing (listed in `missing`), extra chunks, or invalid count/duration

get.summary:
Which chunks the server has acknowledged, so an interrupted or recovered upload sends only
the missing ones. Owner only.

404.description: No such take, or not the caller's

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the chunk's bytes, 64 hex characters.

size_bytes.description: Bytes PUT for this chunk (1 to 16 MiB). Must match the stored object.

url.description: Presigned `PUT` for this chunk's bytes. A bearer credential: don't log it.

allow_download.description: Whether viewers may download the MP4. Defaults to `false`.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 instant after which the link stops working; in the future.

mime_type.description:
The take's MIME type as `MediaRecorder` reports it, e.g. `video/webm;codecs=vp9,opus`.
The container must be `video/webm` or `video/mp4`.

title.description: Optional; blank or missing becomes "Untitled recording". At most 200 characters.

max_duration_ms.description:
The longest take the workspace's plan accepts (pauses excluded). The recorder stops by
itself before this; finalize rejects anything longer.

filename.description: The file name the browser will use.

url.description: A signed URL that saves the MP4; open it (the browser downloads it).

chunk_count.description: Number of chunks in the take; indexes `0..chunk_count` must all be acknowledged.

max_resolution.description: Tallest recording, in pixels of height (1080 = 1080p).

current_workspace_id.description:
The workspace the session's access cookie was issued for -- lets the client pick the
right entry out of `workspaces` as "current" without guessing.

MemberRole.description: Mirrors `kernel::Role` for the OpenAPI schema (kernel stays free of API concerns).

content_type.description:
The video's MIME type, e.g. `video/mp4` or (for a preview) `video/webm`. A browser that
can't play it should keep showing the processing notice.

The adaptive (HLS) master playlist, once the recording's ladder is built: same-origin,
with signed segments behind it. Absent before that (the first view asks for the ladder),

url.description: A signed URL for the video.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

sprite.description: The scrub sprite and its `sprite.vtt` exist.

poster_url.description: A signed thumbnail URL (15 minutes) once the poster exists.

received.description: Acknowledged chunk indexes, ascending. Upload the rest.
